source: npm pack @upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1, tar xzf (not installed/run) in scratchpad adj-docs/upstash-context7-mcp-4.1.1/package/ (tsc output, unminified). Paths below are relative to that package dir. The Context7 API backend is private (README.md:44), so claims about what the backend returns rest on official docs and are tagged [docs]. The remote mcp.context7.com is taken to be this server run with --transport http (package.json scripts.start; RESOURCE_URL default https://mcp.context7.com at dist/lib/constants.js:8). The hosted deployment may run a different build.

resolve-library-id.rationale: The query and libraryName are sent only as query params to the fixed Context7 API, so this is not a SINK. Results are community-submitted library entries, which makes them UNTRUSTED [docs]. With a Context7 credential, results can include the user's teamspace private sources, which is SECRET [docs]; that label is removed when no credential is configured (see value_conditions).
resolve-library-id.evidence: dist/index.js:155-232 (tool registration/handler); dist/lib/api.js:104-111 (new URL(`${CONTEXT7_API_BASE_URL}/v2/libs/search`), searchParams.set only, so the host is not agent-controlled); dist/lib/constants.js:7,10 (base https://context7.com/api); dist/lib/encryption.js:60-62 (credential sent as Authorization: Bearer); README.md:1728 [docs] ('Context7 projects are community-contributed ... cannot guarantee ... security'); https://context7.com/docs/adding-libraries [docs] ('Anyone can add a public library — you don't need to own it'); README.md:56 [docs] ('API Key ... for higher rate limits and private repositories'); https://context7.com/docs/howto/private-sources [docs] (private sources for Pro/Enterprise teams, 'accessible via the API'); dist/lib/utils.js:64 (teamspace-scoped results)

query-docs.rationale: libraryId and query are sent only as query params to the fixed Context7 API (/v2/context), so this is not a SINK. The returned documentation text comes from community-submitted, third-party-maintained libraries, which is UNTRUSTED [docs]. With a credential it can return teamspace private-source documentation, which is SECRET [docs]; that label is removed when no credential is configured.
query-docs.evidence: dist/index.js:233-267 (tool registration/handler returns response.data verbatim); dist/lib/api.js:134-155 (new URL(`${CONTEXT7_API_BASE_URL}/v2/context`), libraryId only via searchParams.set; returns raw text); dist/lib/encryption.js:60-62; README.md:1728 [docs]; README.md:56 [docs]; https://context7.com/docs/howto/private-sources [docs]

value_conditions.effect: Supplies a Context7 credential (stdio only), which enables teamspace private sources and so SECRET on both tools. SECRET is removed from both tools only when this flag AND the CONTEXT7_API_KEY env var, all credential headers, and the /mcp/oauth path are all absent.
value_conditions.default: Absent (along with the other credential conditions): anonymous API access, no private sources, SECRET removed. UNTRUSTED stays.
value_conditions.evidence: dist/index.js:40 (option), dist/index.js:530 (stdioApiKey = cliOptions.apiKey || process.env.CONTEXT7_API_KEY), dist/index.js:85-90 (context), dist/lib/encryption.js:60-62

value_conditions.effect: Same credential as --api-key for stdio, enabling SECRET on both tools. SECRET is removed only when all credential conditions are absent.
value_conditions.default: Absent (along with the other credential conditions): anonymous, SECRET removed.

value_conditions.syntax: Authorization: Bearer <key> | CONTEXT7_API_KEY: <key> | X-Context7-API-Key: <key> | Context7-API-Key: <key> | X-API-Key: <key> | x_api_key: <key>
value_conditions.effect: Credential for HTTP transport / remote mcp.context7.com, forwarded to the API as a Bearer token, enabling SECRET on both tools. SECRET is removed only when all credential conditions are absent.
value_conditions.default: Absent (along with the other credential conditions): anonymous, SECRET removed.

value_conditions.effect: This path forces authentication: requests with no token get 401 and the client runs OAuth, so a credential exists even with no header in the config. SECRET applies to both tools. SECRET is removed only when all credential conditions are absent, i.e. the plain /mcp path with no credential header.
value_conditions.default: Plain /mcp path with no credential header: no auth required, anonymous, SECRET removed.
value_conditions.evidence: dist/index.js:28-34 (requiresAuthentication for /mcp/oauth), dist/index.js:353-389 (401 without token), dist/index.js:420 (route)

notes: Convention for this package: undetermined=false where client code plus official Context7 docs settle the question. Backend behaviour (community provenance, private-source access with a key) is documented but not visible in code, and is tagged [docs].

No SINK: both tools build URLs with new URL(fixed base) and add agent input only through searchParams.set (dist/lib/api.js:106-108, 136-138). No tool fetches an agent-chosen URL. CONTEXT7_API_URL (dist/lib/constants.js:10) can redirect the API base, but only through server config, which the attacker does not control. It does not remove labels.
No host file, database or local network access in tool paths. readFileSync is used only for package.json (constants.js:5) and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (api.js:57-62).

Residual risk for the credential conditions: a stdio server inherits process.env, so CONTEXT7_API_KEY may be present from the user's shell even if the MCP config does not show it. The conditions above treat absence in the config as absence.

Private sources need a Pro/Enterprise plan [docs]. Whether a given credential's teamspace has any cannot be known from config, so the least-restrictive default keeps SECRET whenever a credential is present.
Transport flags --transport/--port and the ?client=claude-code-plugin query do not change tools or labels (dist/index.js:25-34, 38-39).
